title: F12 — the weak-blocks miner and the weak-blocks follower assemble an ordering block's transactions in opposite orders
summary: `CandidateGenerator` mines `previousOrderingBlockTransactions ++ orderingTxs` (CandidateGenerator.scala:771) — the collected input chain FIRST. `ErgoNodeViewHolder.processOrderingBlock` reassembles `orderingBlockTransactions ++ inputBlocksTransactions` (ErgoNodeViewHolder.scala:445) — the input chain LAST — and carries its own `todo: check if ordering block transactions should come first` two lines above. The transactions root is order-sensitive, so the reference follower cannot reconstruct a block the reference miner produced the moment either half is non-empty: it computes a different root and falls back to a full BlockTransactions download. Confirmed against a real mined block, below.

follower.adjacent_comment: // todo: check if ordering block transactions should come first

measured_before_the_fix.why_it_hid: a coinbase-only ordering block has an empty input-chain half, so the two orders coincide and the defect is invisible until the devnet can fund transactions

port_response.behaviour: the planner tries Scala's follower order FIRST, then the candidate order, and only falls back under root_mismatch if neither reproduces the header root. The order that matched is reported as `reconstructed_order` on the /api/v1/events entry and in the debug log, so the split stays measurable instead of being absorbed.
port_response.when_upstream_settles_f12: delete the losing arm of TxOrder

upstream_action: make the two sides agree. The miner's order is the one real blocks hash to, so `processOrderingBlock` is the side to change — or the candidate must be rebuilt to match the follower.
